extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in patent NLP, information retrieval, and AI working on automated patent novelty assessment
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating systems that determine patent claim novelty by decomposing claims into features, retrieving prior-art passages that disclose those features, and reasoning which features are novel to derive claim-level novelty. Emphasis on fine-grained, transparent predictions suitable for practical patent examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-level mapping between claim features and prior-art passages
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty assessment requires intricate matching between specific features of a patent claim and passages in the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should identify which passages in a prior-art document disclose individual claim features (fine-grained mapping), rather than only producing a claim-level label. This mapping supports transparent explanations of why features are novel or anticipated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of claim-level binary classification as sole evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior work has approached novelty prediction primarily as a binary classification task at the claim level, but this formulation is susceptible to spurious correlations and lacks the granularity required for practical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shift evaluation from simple claim-level binary labels to more granular tasks (feature-level retrieval and reasoning). Do not rely solely on claim-level classifiers which can exploit dataset artifacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint retrieval and abstract reasoning evaluation paradigm
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose shifting evaluation to a joint retrieval and abstract reasoning task at the feature level, requiring models to identify specific passages that disclose claim features and to identify which features make a claim novel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should measure both the retrieval quality (are the correct passages found?) and the reasoning/abstraction quality (does the system correctly judge which features are novel based on retrieved evidence?). The final claim-level novelty decision should be derived from feature-level results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset with fine-grained, feature-level prior-art references (FiNE-Patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: FiNE-Patents: a dataset of 3,658 first patent claims annotated with fine-grained, feature-level prior art references extracted from European Search Opinion (ESOP) documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use or compare against FiNE-Patents for training/evaluation when available; annotations are feature-level links to ESOP passages, facilitating passage retrieval and novel-feature identification tasks. Release of dataset enables reproducibility and research into transparent patent analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decomposition workflow requirement (claim -> features -> analysis -> aggregation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement workflows that decompose claims into features, analyze each feature against prior art, and finally derive a claim-level novelty prediction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design systems to explicitly perform decomposition into features, per-feature retrieval/analysis, and a principled aggregation to a claim-level decision. Workflows implemented with LLMs were explored and shown effective in the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics: passage retrieval and novel feature identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments demonstrate that workflows outperform embedding-based baselines on passage retrieval and novel feature identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating systems, report performance on both passage retrieval (e.g., retrieval accuracy/precision/recall/R@k) and novel-feature identification (ability to detect which features are novel). Compare against embedding-based baselines and other relevant baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness to spurious correlations/artifacts
rubrics_metrics.description: LLM-based workflows are robust against spurious correlations present in the claim-level novelty classification task.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate models for robustness to dataset artifacts and spurious correlations (e.g., features that correlate with labels but are not causally informative). Prefer approaches that reason from evidence rather than exploit superficial correlations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and reproducibility via code and data release
rubrics_metrics.description: Release the dataset and code to foster further research into transparent and granular patent analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide dataset and implementation code to enable replication of experiments, inspection of feature-level annotations, and use by others building on this work.
